accepted.question_text: Does there exist a satisfactory structure theory for nondiscrete prodiscrete groups, and more specifically for abelian nondiscrete prodiscrete groups? Here a prodiscrete group means a projective limit of discrete groups, equivalently a closed subgroup of a product of discrete groups.

evidence.quote: Also amongst the pro-Lie groups there are the prodiscrete groups, namely, projective limits of discrete groups or, equivalently, closed subgroups of products of discrete groups. There is not much literature on prodiscrete groups. We formulate the following open question Question 1. Is there a satisfactory structure theory for nondiscrete prodiscrete groups? More particularly, is there a satisfactory structure theory even for abelian nondiscrete prodiscrete groups?

accepted.question_text: If G is a pro-Lie group and G0 is its identity component, must the quotient group G/G0 be complete? Equivalently in the paper's discussion, is G/G0 always prodiscrete?

evidence.quote: The answer to following question is unknown: Question 2. Let G be a pro-Lie group with identity component G0. Is G/G0 complete (and therefore prodiscrete)?

accepted.question_text: Which abelian pro-Lie groups are reflexive under Pontryagin duality, meaning that the canonical evaluation morphism from the group to the double dual is an isomorphism of topological groups?

evidence.quote: Question 3. Which abelian pro-Lie groups are reflexive?

accepted.question_text: Which abelian pro-Lie groups are strongly reflexive, in the sense that every subgroup and every Hausdorff quotient group is reflexive?

evidence.quote: Question 4. Which abelian pro-Lie groups are strongly reflexive in the sense that all of its subgroups and Hausdorff quotient groups are reflexive?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary index set I, is every surjective morphism f: Z^I -> K from the product of copies of the integers onto a compact group K an open map?
accepted.context_brief: Open mapping for Z^I onto compact groups

evidence.quote: Question 5. Is a surjective morphism f : Z I → K onto a compact group open for every set I?
Added in Proof Saak Gabriyelyan and the second author have recently announced a positive answer to Question 5.

accepted.question_text: Is there a more elaborate duality theory relating real Hopf algebras and weakly complete Hopf algebras in which the pro-Lie group and pro-Lie algebra facts described in the paper play an essential role, and does the existence of weakly complete enveloping algebras of weakly complete Lie algebras imply that for every pro-Lie algebra L there is an associative weakly complete Hopf algebra U(L) such that L is isomorphic to a closed Lie subalgebra of the primitive elements P(U(L))?
accepted.context_brief: Hopf algebra duality and enveloping algebras

evidence.quote: Question 6. (i) Is there a more elaborate duality theory of real Hopf algebras and weakly complete Hopf algebras in which these facts on pro-Lie group and pro-Lie algebra theory play a role? (ii) Does the existence of weakly complete enveloping algebras of weakly complete Lie algebras secure for each pro-Lie algebra L an associative weakly complete Hopf Algebra U(L) such that L is isomorphic to a closed Lie subalgebra of P(U(L))?

accepted.question_text: If an abelian prodiscrete group is compactly generated and has no nondegenerate compact subgroups, must it be discrete?

evidence.quote: Question 7. Is an abelian prodiscrete compactly generated group without nondegenerate compact subgroups a discrete group?

accepted.question_text: If an abelian prodiscrete group is compactly generated and compact-free, meaning that it has no nontrivial compact subgroups, must it be a finitely generated free abelian group?

evidence.quote: Question 8. Is a compactly generated abelian prodiscrete compact–free group a finitely generated free abelian group? Note that by compact-free we mean the group has no nontrivial compact subgroups.

accepted.question_text: In an arbitrary real semisimple Lie algebra, is every element equal to a single Lie bracket [x,y] for some pair of elements x and y?
accepted.context_brief: Bracket generation in semisimple Lie algebras

evidence.quote: Question 9. Is every element in an arbitrary real semisimple Lie algebra a bracket?

accepted.question_text: Is every transfinitely nilpotent connected pro-Lie group pronilpotent?

evidence.quote: Question 10. Is a transfinitely nilpotent connected pro-Lie group pronilpotent?

accepted.question_text: Is there a satisfactory theory of Polish pro-Lie groups, separable pro-Lie groups, or compactly generated pro-Lie groups, especially in the connected case?
accepted.context_brief: Polish, separable, and compactly generated pro-Lie groups

evidence.quote: Question 12. Is there a satisfactory theory of Polish pro-Lie groups (respectively, separable pro-Lie groups, or compactly generated pro-Lie groups), notably, in the connected case?

evidence.quote: Question 11. Let h be a closed subalgebra of the Lie algebra g of a connected pro-Lie group G. Let A(h) denote the analytic group generated by h. Is A(h)/A(h) abelian? (See [17], Theorem 9.32.)
